observations: Photo 0 and 1 show the same Yamaha keyboard wrapped in clear plastic film.
The keyboard has a blue control panel with a digital display and buttons.
The brand 'YAMAHA' is visible on the bottom right of the panel in photo 0.
The model 'KEYBOARD 200' is visible on the bottom left of the panel in photo 0.
The keyboard has 61 keys (37 white and 24 black).
The plastic wrapping is visible on the right side of the keyboard in both photos.
The seller's text mentions 'Very good sound and quality Yamaha keyboard' and 'adapter included'.
No power adapter or cables are visible in the photos.

claims.claim: Very good sound and quality Yamaha keyboard
claims.evidence: Sound cannot be tested from still photos; the seller's claim is subjective.
No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.
No adapter is visible in the photos.

claims.claim: Bought from the UK, no dead key, no crackle
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The keyboard may not power on or produce sound.
risks.proof: A video of the keyboard powered on and playing a song.

risks.risk: The plastic wrapping may be damaged or the keyboard may be scratched.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the keyboard surface and the edges of the plastic wrap.

risks.risk: The keyboard may have dead keys or internal faults.
risks.proof: A video of the keyboard being played through a tuner or audio app.

risks.risk: The power adapter may be missing or damaged.
risks.proof: A photo of the power adapter and the cables.

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Video of the keyboard powered on and playing a song.
Close-up photos of the keyboard surface and the edges of the plastic wrap.
Photo of the power adapter and the cables.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
